prs.title: fix(client): release SSE reader locks
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the identical bug: the SSE reader obtained via `.getReader()` in the streamable HTTP client's response-reading loop is never released when the stream ends or the connection drops, so the reader-tied internal buffer (~50MB for long-lived clients) can't be garbage-collected. Both diffs are against the same base line (streamableHttp.ts index 736587973d..) and make the exact same structural change: wrapping the `while (true) { reader.read() ... }` loop in a try block so the lock is released afterward. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the same Accept-header check in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts's POST handler. #1996 adds a dedicated `acceptsMediaType` helper that does spec-correct parsing: splits on `;` params, ignores entries with `q=0`, and matches type/subtype (including wildcards). #2046 instead uses a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check, which has no q-value handling and can false-positive on unrelated subtypes containing that substring (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`). #1996's approach handles more real-world Accept header variations correctly.

clusters.pick_reason: #2215 fixes the same trailing-slash normalization in buildWellKnownPath but also carries the fix through to shouldAttemptFallback, changing its root check from `pathname === '/'` to `pathname === ''` via a new shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper — without this, the root-path fallback check goes stale once trailing slashes are stripped, causing a redundant fallback attempt on root-like paths. #2214 applies the same regex fix in two call sites (buildWellKnownPath and buildDiscoveryUrls) but does not update shouldAttemptFallback, so if merged alone it leaves that redundant-fallback behavior unfixed. #2214's extra buildDiscoveryUrls edit is not covered by #2215 and should be folded in on top of #2215 by whoever merges it.

clusters.pick_reason: #2692's close() settles outstanding requests with a proper per-request-id JSON-RPC error (-32000 'Connection closed'), explicitly groups outstanding ids by stream to handle batched POSTs (one stream can carry several request ids), and skips ids that already have a real response so it never clobbers a completed result. #2600 settles the same parked POSTs with a single blanket 404 'Session not found' response, which doesn't address per-request-id batching and mislabels a mid-flight close as a missing session. #2600 additionally clears `_requestToStreamMapping` to fix a separate correlation-leak bug in send()/storeEvent() racing with close() - that part is not a duplicate of #2692 and should be re-filed/reapplied on top of #2692 rather than lost when #2600 is closed.
